title: Routing-aware usage metering and realtime SLO enforcement for console analytics ingest
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Goal: build a routing-aware metering/enrichment pipeline that directly correlates ingest-level events (token counts, route id, model variant, latency, errors) to per-route SLIs and a realtime enforcement engine. This ticket covers schema design, enrichment service, storage for fast SLO queries, and a lightweight enforcer that can apply throttles or fallback policies when SLOs are at risk.

Why now: customers are asking for finer-grain cost attribution and predictable SLOs by route/model. Current analytics only provides daily rollups; we need sub-minute visibility to trigger graceful fallbacks (model downgrade or burst cap) and accurate billing for Dedicated customers.

Outcomes: (1) per-route token and request counters with 1m resolution, (2) real-time SLO windows (1m/5m/1h) for latency and error rate, (3) integration with Console rollouts to automatically apply fallback policies when a route's SLO breaches, (4) dashboards and alerts for operators and product managers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Enrichment service consumes existing ingest topic and emits enriched events with route_id, tenant_id, model_tag, token_count, latency_ms, error_class, and sample_key.
2) Materialized store exposes APIs for SLI windows (1m/5m/1h) with >99% availability and query p95 < 200ms for single-route queries.
3) SLO enforcer can evaluate policies and apply a fallback to a lower-cost model variant within 30s of breach detection in canary mode.
4) Grafana dashboard panels for per-route token-rate, 99p latency, and error-rate exist and linked.
5) Rollout can be toggled per-tenant and scoped by route via feature flag.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: Kafka ingest -> Enrichment service (Go) -> stream-aggregation (Flink/Beam) -> materialized store (ClickHouse or Druid) + short-lived cache (Redis) for 1m lookups -> SLO enforcer service that subscribes to aggregated notifications.

Schema notes: Use a compact event with hashed tenant_id and route_id (sha1 prefix) to limit cardinality in downstream. Include model_tag and quantization_profile as optional strings. Token_count as int, latency_ms as int, error_code as string. Add deterministic sample_key for consistent sampling.

Scaling/tradeoffs: Full-cardinality per-tenant per-route storage at 1m resolution is expensive. We'll use two-tier aggregation: exact counters for top 1000 routes (by traffic) and an approximate count-min sketch for the tail. This preserves accuracy where it matters while bounding storage.

Data retention: 1m resolution for 7 days, 5m resolution for 30 days, 1h resolution for 90 days. Longer retention for billing aggregates only.

Privacy/security: PII-free events. Tenant hashing and KMS encryption in transit. No raw prompts or payload tokens are stored. Security review not required for this change (config-only), but UA will be consulted for Dedicated customers.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal canary: enable for internal tenant + 1 staging tenant (1% of routes) for 48h.
2) Canary v1: select 10 production tenants with low-risk routes for 7 days, monitor SLI drift and backpressure events.
3) Canary v2: expand to 30 tenants / 10% routes.
4) Global: toggle on by default for new tenants, opt-in for legacy tenants.
5) Fallback behavior introduced behind a feature flag and a kill switch in Console.

Observability during rollout: synthetic probes per route, end-to-end traces, and a rollback runbook if error-rate increases >2x baseline or token-metering mismatch >0.5%.
metrics_and_dashboards: Console: Metering Healthboard - counts vs billing pipeline (daily)
testing_plan:
Unit tests for enrichment logic and sampling determinism. End-to-end test using replayed production events in staging to validate counts and SLO calculations. Load test to 2x current peak ingest with representative tenant cardinality. Fault-injection tests for Kafka lag and downstream ClickHouse failures.

Pre-merge checklist: schema migration strategy, monitoring alerts created, dashboard smoke tests green.
security_and_compliance_notes: Events contain no user content. Tenant ids are hashed; KMS used for service-to-service authentication. Dedicated customers can opt into on-prem metric retention. Audit logs for enforcer actions recorded in Console audit stream.
notes_on_edge_cases:
- Late-arriving events: allow 2m window correction and backfill reconciler job for hourly rollups.
- Duplicates: use event_id dedupe in enrichment service keyed by Kafka offset and event id.
- High-cardinality tenants: promote to exact counters when a tenant crosses 99p route traffic threshold, tracked by monitor.

2025-01-20 | Ravi Menon: Design doc uploaded to Confluence. Flagging decision: ClickHouse for materialized store due to fast single-route queries; Druid considered but rejected for complex rollups cost. See design link.
2025-01-27 | PM Ana Lopez: PM review - need to ensure billing alignment with usage counters; added requirement to compare daily aggregates against billing pipeline (end of day reconciliation).

2025-02-04 | SRE Marcus Chen: Concern about spiky backpressure from enforcer hitting downstream rate limits. Proposed adding token-bucket smoothing and graceful fallback to model-variant downgrades rather than hard throttles.
2025-02-12 | Security review (Lina Alvarez): Confirmed no sensitive data stored; recommend adding tenant-hash salt rotation policy. Will follow up separately.
